definition: The ontological structure of human freedom experienced as sympathetic antipathy toward the nothingness of future possibilities; not a pathological condition but the awareness of one's capacity to choose, famously described as the dizziness of freedom (Svimmelhed) when confronting the open abyss of possibility
connective_patterns: anxiety as the dizziness of freedom
anxiety before the possibility of possibility
anxiety is the reality of freedom as possibility before this possibility has materialized

definition: The decisive non-rational commitment by which an individual entrusts themselves to the absolute (God), embracing paradox and objective uncertainty; not a conclusion of rational deliberation but an act of passionate inwardness that transitions from the ethical to the religious sphere
connective_patterns: the leap from the ethical to the religious
faith requires the leap into objective uncertainty
the leap as the category of decision

definition: The existential structure of radical choice between incommensurable life-orientations (aesthetic vs. ethical); one cannot think one's way from one sphere to another — the transition requires an act of will that constitutes the choosing self, making the choice itself more fundamental than what is chosen
connective_patterns: either/or as the nerve of all existence
the choice that constitutes the self
not what one chooses but that one chooses

definition: A forward-looking existential category contrasted with Platonic recollection; whereas recollection seeks to recover a lost past, repetition is the movement by which the self re-attains itself through renewed commitment, gaining the same thing again but in a transformed mode — the existential analogue of faith's renewal
connective_patterns: repetition as recollection forwards
repetition and the religious stage
what is repeated is not the same but the renewed

term: stages on life's way/人生阶段
definition: A typology of three existence-spheres — aesthetic, ethical, and religious — through which human life orients itself; not a developmental sequence that unfolds automatically but qualitatively distinct modes of existing, with transitions requiring crisis and decisive choice rather than gradual progress
connective_patterns: the three stages as aesthetic, ethical, and religious
boundary zones of irony and humor between stages
each stage is a self-contained way of life

definition: The existence-sphere defined by the pursuit of immediate pleasure, intellectual enjoyment, and sensuous desire; the aesthete lives in the moment, interprets themselves as if on stage, avoids commitment, and seeks the interesting — a life that is, whether the aesthete knows it or not, one of complete despair
connective_patterns: the aesthetic as the ceaseless pursuit of the interesting
the aesthete's despair beneath the surface
rotation method as the aesthete's strategy

definition: The existence-sphere defined by commitment, duty, and self-determination through universal moral law; the ethical individual takes ownership of past and present, discovers a deeper concept of selfhood through responsible choice, and constitutes their identity through sustained fidelity to commitments (paradigmatically marriage)
connective_patterns: the ethical as the sphere of the universal
the ethical self constituted through commitment
the teleological suspension of the ethical in Fear and Trembling

definition: The existence-sphere defined by absolute relation to the absolute; the religious individual stands before God as the single individual, beyond the universal claims of ethics — exemplified by Abraham's willingness to sacrifice Isaac, where faith demands what ethics forbids, revealing the paradox at the heart of religious existence
connective_patterns: the religious as absolute relation to the absolute
the knight of faith vs. the knight of infinite resignation
the paradox of Abraham and the teleological suspension of the ethical

definition: The sickness unto death — a mis-relation in the self's relation to itself, wherein the self is unwilling either to be itself or to be the self God intends; ranges from unconscious despair (not knowing one has a self) to defiant despair (willing to be a self on one's own terms), and can only be overcome through faith
connective_patterns: despair as the sickness unto death
despair of not willing to be oneself
despair of willing to be oneself defiantly

definition: Den Enkelte — the single, existing individual who stands before God in irreducible singularity, not absorbed into the crowd, the public, or the system; the category Kierkegaard considered his most important contribution, opposing the leveling tendency of the age and the abstraction of Hegelian philosophy
connective_patterns: the individual as the category of spirit
the crowd is untruth
truth is subjectivity as the individual's inward relation

definition: A stance of feigned ignorance and existential distancing inherited from Socrates; irony enables critical reflection and detachment from the immediate, serving as the boundary zone between the aesthetic and ethical stages — but risks becoming infinite irony that never commits to anything, dissolving all content into playful negation
connective_patterns: irony as the boundary between the aesthetic and the ethical
irony as mastered moment vs. infinite irony
the ironist as midwife of subjectivity

definition: Kierkegaard's method of using pseudonyms, fiction, irony, and multiple authorial voices to communicate existential truths without violating the reader's subjectivity; direct statement of subjective truths leads to passive reception, so indirect communication forces the reader to appropriate the meaning personally through their own existential engagement
connective_patterns: indirect communication as respect for the reader's subjectivity
the pseudonymous authorship as indirect communication
communication of capability vs. communication of knowledge

definition: Øjeblikket — the decisive instant in which eternity intersects with time, the temporal becomes the vessel of the eternal; not mere chronological succession but the qualitative atom of existential decision where the individual confronts the absolute and the possibility of radical transformation
connective_patterns: the moment as the intersection of time and eternity
the moment of decision
the moment as the atom of eternity within time

definition: An early English rendering of Angst emphasizing the uncanny, objectless character of existential anxiety; unlike fear which has a determinate object, dread is the feeling of being threatened without knowing whence the danger arises — it paralyzes the senses and confronts the individual with the groundlessness of freedom
connective_patterns: dread as desire for what one fears
dread before the nothing of possibility
sympathetic antipathy and antipathetic sympathy
